items.title: Thunder’s Thomas Sorber Undergoes Another Knee Surgery
items.summary: Thunder center Thomas Sorber’s NBA debut has been delayed once again. Sorber underwent an arthroscopic procedure on Tuesday to address inflammation at the patellofemoral joint in his right knee, the team tweets. The issue developed in the late stages of his return-to-play process. He’s expected to return to on-court activities in six-to-eight weeks. Sorber, who suffered a torn ACL in his right knee in September 2025, appeared close to suiting up for the injury-riddled Thunder. Last week, coach Mark Daigneault expressed optimism regarding Sorber’s possible return. “He’s done an incredible job of just working through this ramp-up and his journey back to the floor. … He’s got his head down. And when he’s ready, we’ll get him out there. And I can’t wait to do that because he deserves it,” Daigneault said. Sorber underwent another arthroscopic procedure on the same knee in July. items.title: Grizzlies’ GG Jackson Undergoes Foot Surgery, Out Minimum Of Three Months
items.summary: Nov. 17: Jackson underwent surgery on Tuesday to repair a broken metatarsal in his left foot, according to the team (Twitter link). He will be reevaulated in approximately three months. Nov. 16: Grizzlies forward GG Jackson II will undergo surgery after breaking the fifth metatarsal bone in his left foot, the team announced today (via Twitter). A return timeline won’t be established until the procedure is complete, but if Jackson’s injury history is any indication, he’ll likely miss most of the 2026/27 season. Jackson broke the fifth metatarsal bone in his right foot a little over two years ago and underwent surgery on September 4, 2024. He didn’t make his 2024/25 debut until January 20, 2025 — roughly four-and-a-half months later. If Jackson is out four-and-a-half months this time around, he wouldn’t return to action until late March/early April. The regular season ends on April 11.…

items.title: Hawks’ Asa Newell Undergoes Toe Surgery, Out Four Months
items.summary: Hawks forward Asa Newell, who sustained a left great toe hyperextension earlier this month, was reevaluated on Monday by a specialist, meeting with Dr. Martin O’Malley in New York, according to the team. Newell underwent additional imaging during that reevaluation that confirmed the hyperextension and also revealed a plantar plate tear in the affected toe. The 21-year-old underwent surgery on Tuesday to treat that injury and is expected to miss most of the rest of the season while he recovers. According to the Hawks, Newell will be reevaluated in approximately four months, which means he’s unlikely to return until mid-to-late March at the earliest. The regular season ends on April 11. It’s an unfortunate setback for Newell, who had been hoping to earn a more consistent rotation role at the NBA level this season after frequently being assigned to the G League during his rookie year.
